text:
olivia: Kicking off the DeltaHealth POC perf run. Goal: sustained 600 qps, p95 < 120ms for ~1k token responses. Need test window + cost estimate. Proposing a 2-hour soak + a 10-min spike. @maria can you confirm customer allowed regions (us-west only for now)?

maria: Confirmed — they want us-west only for initial POC. Also asked for SLA wording and an estimated committed capacity number. :+1:

kevin: For the harness I'd use rwi-load v2.1 (our in-house runner). It does KV cache warmup + realistic prompt length mix. I'll paste the run config. Use 8 concurrent clients per GPU; target ~100 qps per client for steady-state burst math. Route through dedicated-dev pool to avoid noisy neighbors.

zack: Dedicated-dev runs on A100-80GB nodes. For ~1k token outputs use seq_len=1024 plan. Recommend trying q8_128 quant first — should drop memory and keep perf. If customer insists on fp16 we can switch but expect ~1.9x compute cost.

maria: Customer asked for a rough cost estimate to include in the deck. Can we give a ballpark before the run?

kevin: Rough compute: at 600 qps sustained with q8 model, GPU utilization ~78% per A100. We'll need ~4 GPUs to hit sustained throughput with headroom (+ autoscale buffer). Rough committed price estimate ~ $XXk/mo — I'll finalize numbers after the soak.

olivia: Here's the run config (kevin pls verify):
```
# rwi-load config
model: redwood-q8-13b
seq_len: 1024
clients: 8
target_qps: 600
duration: 2h
spike: {duration: 600, qps: 1200}
payload_distribution: { short: 45, medium: 35, long: 20 }
```
Link to harness/configs: https://internal.redwood/s3/deltahealth/poc-configs

kevin: LGTM. I'll run a quick smoke now then the full soak at 15:00 PST.

deploy-bot: run-2140002001 started by kevin — rwi-load smoke (10m) on dedicated-dev :rocket:

kevin: Smoke done. No OOMs, p95 ~95ms at 150 qps. Proceeding to full soak.

deploy-bot: run-2140003000 started by kevin — rwi-load soak (2h) on dedicated-dev

kevin: Soak finished. Quick summary: 
- sustained avg throughput: 610 qps
- p50: 32ms
- p95: 112ms
- p99: 258ms
- errors: 0.04% (mostly transient timeouts during spike)
Full metrics & traces: https://internal.redwood/s3/deltahealth/poc-results/2140003000

maria: Nice — p95 is under the target. Customer will ask about the p99 tail and mitigations. :thinking:

zack: Tail looks like occasional host-side batching GC + CPU throttling on the rpc-proxy during spikes. Quick mitigations: bump batch_timeout -> 12ms, increase proxy CPU to 2vCPU, and enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts. Should cut p99 by ~30%.

kevin: I re-ran a 10-min burst with batch_timeout=12ms and proxy CPU increased — p99 dropped from 258ms -> 184ms. I'll write up a follow-up run and update cost estimates (GPU hours + proxy sizing).

olivia: Next steps: kevin to produce final run writeup + cost calc, maria to send the customer summary with p95/p99 notes and recommended fallback (q8 model + prefix cache + A/B with fp16 if needed). Aim to share by EOD. :tada:

maria: I'll draft the email and include the attached results link. If kevin can drop the final numbers by 3pm PST that would be perfect.

kevin: Will do — putting the writeup in the same S3 folder and pinging here when done.

zack: If they want lower p99 we can also propose a small dedicated headroom pool for spikes (burst nodes) — cheaper than full commit to hit 1200 qps spikes.

olivia: Good call. We'll include that as an option in the pricing sheet. Thanks all!
